title: Design a Chess / Tic-Tac-Toe Game
relevance: High — flagship board-game LLD pair; Tic-Tac-Toe is the warm-up / machine-coding staple (Flipkart, Uber, Amazon, Microsoft), Chess is the harder OOD probe (piece polymorphism, legality, Command undo) at Amazon/Microsoft/Meta-style loops.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad machine-coding opener as Tic-Tac-Toe (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon, Razorpay); experienced/SDE-2 probes Chess or TTT with N×N + Strategy + Bot; FAANG OOD whiteboard for Design Chess / Design Tic-Tac-Toe; among the most asked game LLDs.

phases.goal: Lock functional scope for TTT and/or Chess, plus NFRs and clarifying assumptions before design.

must_hit.point: Tic-Tac-Toe mandatory FR: N×N board (default 3), two players X/O alternate, reject occupied/OOB cells, detect win (row/col/diag) and draw (full board), print board after valid moves.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists place-mark, validation, win/draw detection, and board print without jumping to class names.

must_hit.point: Chess mandatory FR: 8×8 board, White/Black with White first, place standard 16+16 pieces, validate piece moves, alternate turns, at least sketch checkmate/stalemate detection.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states two-color turn loop, piece placement, move validation, and terminal check/mate/stale outcomes.

must_hit.point: Clarify before coding: TTT size/win-length/players/Bot/undo/CLI I/O; Chess full FIDE vs subset, specials (castling, en passant, promotion), clocks, undo, resign/draw.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks scoping questions and explicitly calls out which specials or extensions are in/out of scope.

must_hit.point: NFR: modular files (not one god class), extensible rules, correct under concurrent move attempts if multi-client, working CLI demo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions modularity/extensibility and optionally concurrent-move correctness without overbuilding product features.

probes: What are the mandatory functional requirements for Tic-Tac-Toe vs Chess, and which extensions will you defer?
Will you implement full FIDE specials, or a subset with hooks—and how does that affect the CLI demo?

hints.1: Start by listing what must work in a happy-path CLI before optional Bot or castling.
hints.2: Separate TTT place/validate/win-draw/print from Chess place/validate/turn/terminal-status checklists.
hints.3: Mandatory TTT: N×N (default 3), X/O alternate, reject bad cells, win/draw, print; mandatory Chess: 8×8, White first, 16+16 pieces, validate moves, sketch mate/stalemate.

phases.goal: Name the shared turn-based skeleton and the distinct TTT vs Chess domain objects.

must_hit.point: Shared skeleton: Game orchestrator + Board + Player + Move + terminal status for both turn-based board games.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Game, Board, Player, Move, and a status concept before diving into piece types.

must_hit.point: Core TTT entities: Board (grid + place/validate), Player (name + symbol), PlayingPiece/Symbol, Game (turns + outcome); optional WinningStrategy and Deque of Player for round-robin.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists Board/Player/Symbol/Game and may mention WinningStrategy or Deque for multi-player turns.

must_hit.point: Core Chess entities: abstract Piece → King/Queen/Rook/Bishop/Knight/Pawn; Board as 8×8 of Square/Box; Move (from/to + captured + flags); Player (color); Game/ChessGame (turn, status, history).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows Piece hierarchy, Square/Box cells, Move with capture/flags, and Game owning turn/status/history.

must_hit.point: Status models: TTT GameStatus IN_PROGRESS | WIN | DRAW; Chess ACTIVE | CHECK | CHECKMATE | STALEMATE | RESIGNED | DRAW.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Enumerates terminal/in-progress statuses for the game being designed rather than inventing unrelated states.

probes: What objects appear in both games, and what is unique to Chess’s Piece hierarchy?
How do you model Move and GameStatus differently for TTT undo vs Chess capture/special flags?

hints.1: Both games are turn-based—name the shared orchestrator pieces first.
hints.2: Map TTT to Board/Player/Symbol/Game(+WinningStrategy); Chess to Piece subclasses, Square/Box, Move, colored Player.
hints.3: Say: Game+Board+Player+Move+status for both; Chess adds abstract Piece→six concretes and Move flags for castle/en passant/promotion.

phases.goal: Assign responsibilities and patterns so Game stays a facade and movement/win rules stay swappable.

must_hit.point: Game is facade/controller: owns turn, status, history, public makeMove; does not embed piece geometry or win-line formulas inline when Strategy is expected.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes Game coordinating makeMove while Board/Piece/Strategy own grid and rules.

must_hit.point: Do not put movement switch(pieceType) in Board/Game—each Piece subclass owns geometry (OCP for fairy pieces / Chess960 stretch).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Puts canMove/getPseudoLegalMoves on Piece hierarchy instead of a central type switch.

must_hit.point: Patterns that earn points: Strategy (win/AI/Human vs Bot), Command (Move execute/undo + history), State/status enum, Factory (pieces/players), Template Method or polymorphism on Piece.canMove, Observer (UI/scoreboard).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least Strategy and Command (or Piece polymorphism) and where they plug into Game.

must_hit.point: API surface: TTT create_game/make_move/get_board/undo; LeetCode-shaped TicTacToe(n)/move→0|1|2; Chess Game.start/makeMove, Piece.canMove, Board.isSquareAttacked, Game.isInCheck/isCheckmate/isStalemate, Move.execute/undo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches makeMove-style APIs and Chess legality helpers without inventing unrelated endpoints.

probes: Where does piece movement validation live, and why not a switch in Game?
Which patterns would you use for win rules, Human vs Bot, and undoable moves?

hints.1: Think facade Game vs grid Board vs rule owners.
hints.2: WinningStrategy/PlayerStrategy and Piece.canMove keep Game thin; Command backs undo history.
hints.3: Game.makeMove orchestrates; Piece subclasses own geometry; Strategy for win/AI input; Command stack for undo.

phases.goal: Explain TTT win detection and the Chess legality pipeline including check filtering.

must_hit.point: TTT win detection: naive scan all lines after each move is fine for 3×3; senior bar is O(1) with +1/−1 row/col/diag counters (LeetCode 348); for N×N with K-in-a-row check lines through last move (O(N) or O(K)).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes either full-line scan for 3×3 or incremental counters, and last-move line check for larger boards.

must_hit.point: Chess move pipeline: (1) own piece + turn, (2) piece geometry canMove, (3) path clear for sliders, (4) destination empty or enemy, (5) simulate and reject if own king remains in check, (6) commit + evaluate check/mate/stalemate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks ordered validation ending in simulate-for-self-check then terminal evaluation.

must_hit.point: Separate pseudo-legal from legal moves; geometry-only validators miss self-check—always simulate-or-filter.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines pseudo-legal as geometry/path and legal as surviving the king-safety filter.

must_hit.point: Checkmate = in check + zero legal moves; stalemate = not in check + zero legal moves.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts mate vs stalemate solely by whether the side to move is currently in check.

probes: How would you detect a TTT win in O(1), and what changes for K-in-a-row on N×N?
Walk through validating a Chess move from turn check through rejecting moves that leave your king in check.

hints.1: TTT: scanning lines is fine on a small board; Chess: geometry alone is not enough.
hints.2: Mention row/col/diag counters for TTT and a simulate step before committing Chess moves.
hints.3: Pipeline: turn+ownership → canMove → path clear → capture rules → simulate self-check → commit and classify mate/stalemate.

phases.goal: Show how new board sizes, players, bots, pieces, and undo plug in without editing Game’s core.

must_hit.point: SOLID signal: OCP = new piece / win strategy / bot without editing Game; SRP = Board holds cells, Piece validates geometry, Game owns turns + legality filter; DIP on Piece/WinningStrategy/PlayerStrategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains adding a piece or Bot via subclass/strategy without rewriting Game’s turn loop.

must_hit.point: Extensions: parameterize N×N / K-in-a-row / P players with Deque turns; PlayerStrategy Human vs Bot (random/minimax); Command undo reversing board cells and TTT counters or Chess captured piece & flags.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Avoids hardcoding 2 players or fixed 3×3 in Game and describes Strategy/Command hooks for Bot/undo.

must_hit.point: Chess specials as Move subtypes or flags tracking hasMoved, lastMove, promote on last rank; implement promotion + castling hooks if time; en passant needs lastMove metadata—don’t claim full FIDE if only basics done.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Hooks specials via Move flags/metadata and is honest about subset vs full rules.

probes: How do you support N×N, three players, and a Bot without rewriting Game?
How would undo and castling/en passant/promotion attach to your Move model?

hints.1: Ask what should change when board size or player count grows.
hints.2: WinningStrategy, Deque turns, and PlayerStrategy keep Game stable; Command restores prior board state.
hints.3: Parameterize size/players; Strategy for win/Bot; Command stack for undo; special Move flags with hasMoved/lastMove for chess specials.

phases.goal: State single-threaded CLI default and how shared online game objects serialize moves.

must_hit.point: Local CLI is single-threaded; concurrency matters when framing online/shared game object.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says CLI demo needs no locks, then addresses shared-instance races if multi-client is in scope.

must_hit.point: If online/shared game object: serialize makeMove (one lock per game / synchronized makeMove); never let two clients mutate the same board.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Proposes per-game locking around makeMove and server-side validation rather than client-trusted boards.

must_hit.point: Multi-game server: one Game instance per match id; lock per game, not global; Chess clocks/network are product stretch—mention server-side validation, don’t implement mid-round.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Scopes concurrency to per-match Game locks and defers clocks/network implementation.

probes: Does your CLI need synchronization, and what changes if two clients share one Game?
Where do you put the lock in a multi-match server?

hints.1: Local demo vs shared online object are different concurrency stories.
hints.2: Think one lock around makeMove for a shared Game, not a process-wide lock.
hints.3: CLI single-threaded; shared Game uses synchronized/per-game lock on makeMove; one Game per match id.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Full scan is OK for 3×3 demos; row/col/diag counters or last-move line checks show you scale when N grows (LeetCode 348 / N×N with K-in-a-row) without changing the Game API.

tradeoffs.topic: Inheritance vs Strategy for Chess movement
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Subclass-per-piece is the classic answer; Strategy-per-movement-style (slide/leap/pawn) reduces duplication for Queen as Rook∪Bishop—either is fine if justified and Board/Game stay free of piece-type switches.
Geometry-only validators miss self-check; always simulate-or-filter. Checkmate = in check + zero legal moves; stalemate = not in check + zero legal moves.
Enum plus guarded transitions is enough for interviews; full State objects only if behavior per status grows (e.g. reject moves after mate).

Implement promotion + castling hooks if time; note en passant needs lastMove metadata; do not claim full FIDE if only basics were coded—mandatory validate, alternate turns, and terminal detection come first.

gotchas.trap: Hardcoding 2 players or 3×3 constants in Game when asked for N×N / 3 players
gotchas.correction: Parameterize board size; use Deque for turns; keep player count and win length configurable.
Maintain +1/−1 row/col/diag counters; win when abs equals N (or winLength).

gotchas.trap: Adding a Bot by editing Game’s turn loop
gotchas.correction: Introduce PlayerStrategy / BotPlayer (e.g. minimax); Game only asks nextMove(board).

gotchas.trap: Undo that only clears a cell
gotchas.correction: Use a Command stack; reverse board cell plus TTT counters or Chess captured piece and special-move flags.

gotchas.trap: Skipping king-safety after a geometrically valid move
gotchas.correction: Simulate on a copy (or make/unmake); reject if own king remains in check.

gotchas.trap: Treating checkmate and stalemate as the same
gotchas.correction: Both mean zero legal moves; mate additionally requires currently being in check.

gotchas.trap: God-class Game with giant switch on piece type / win lines
gotchas.correction: Docks OCP—push geometry to Piece subclasses and win rules to WinningStrategy.

gotchas.trap: Finishing optional AI/specials but failing mandatory validate + alternate turns + terminal detection
gotchas.correction: Ship mandatory path first; specials and AI are stretch.

gotchas.trap: workat.tech wrong print format or continuing after win
gotchas.correction: Read the I/O contract carefully; stop announcing further turns once the game is over.
